# Silent-link inventory -- declared, defined nowhere, referenced by nothing

<!-- GENERATED by tools/re/silent_link_sweep.py -- do not hand-edit the tables. -->
b5-decomp rev `87ae93150`.

A function the console CALLS, declared in our headers, DEFINED NOWHERE, and referenced by
nothing **links in complete silence** -- no compiler warning, no linker error, no assert,
no log line. There is no reference for the linker to fail on, so nothing in the toolchain
can see it. Three player-visible bugs of this exact shape landed in one session:
`ParticleModule::EndOfFrame` (#17, `c227a165`), `UpdateRecoveringFromSlam` (#14,
`51cd862d`), and `GuiModule::EndOfFrame` (`2f0e038a`).

## The companion snapshot: `progress/sweep/silent_declarations.json`

A **declaration-first** pass over the same question, run earlier the same day against the
working tree at `465fa81b`. It is a frozen snapshot -- its generator was not kept, so it
does not regenerate and must not be read as current. It is retained for the two axes this
tool does not produce:

* **`bucket not-in-console` (2,312)** -- declarations in OUR headers for which the ARTIST
  export has no function at all. Candidate **inventions**, the mirror of this inventory.
* **`dropped_has_call_site` (1,154)** -- a declaration with no body that our tree
  nonetheless *calls*. It only links because the calling TU is not mounted; mounting that
  TU turns each into an unresolved external.

It also carries 12 positive controls and two blind spots worth repeating here: **ICF
folding** (identical one-line console bodies are folded, so IDA can print a neighbour's
name on the fold target) and **macros** (a call generated by a macro body is invisible to a
text call index). And it quantifies the class-C caveat: **25.3% of all 30,084 console
functions have no `xrefs_to` at all**.

## What this evidence CANNOT distinguish

1. **Class C is not "uncalled".** Virtual dispatch is invisible to `xrefs_to` (above).
2. **"Mounted" is not "executed".** The exe compiles the caller in; whether that caller
   runs is a separate question. Only the `ran at boot` column is evidence of execution, and
   it comes from a 30 s boot-to-main-menu Xenia trace (`progress/goals.json`,
   `boot-trace.executed_funcs`, 1,880 functions) -- so a blank cell means *not proven*, not
   *not executed*. Nothing here proves an in-race gameplay path runs.
3. **An absent call may have been INLINED into the caller by hand.** The sweep asks whether
   a definition exists, not whether the behaviour does. Read the caller before fixing.
4. **A name match is a name match.** Matching falls back to the last two components
   (`Class::Method`), so a name shared by two unrelated classes can mask one of them.
   5 of the 14 class-A caller edges are double-confirmed against the CALLER's own
   `xrefs_from`; the 9 that are not are name collisions of this kind -- check those rows
   by hand.
5. **Overload sets collapse.** A class with two `SetScore` overloads, one defined and one
   not, reads as defined.
6. **Ownership flags are inferred from issue TITLES only** (#9 "minimap: no blips", #11
   "in-game events UI"); the issue text was not available to this sweep.

## Regenerating / the positive control

```
python tools/re/silent_link_sweep.py            # rewrite progress/silent_link_inventory.*
python tools/re/silent_link_sweep.py --control  # prove the sweep can still FIND a known one
```

`--control` re-runs the whole sweep against the tree at b5 `488e7e82` (= `c227a165^`, the
commit *before* the tyre-mark fix) and asserts the seed bugs come back out of it. It
currently reports both `ParticleModule::EndOfFrame` and `UpdateRecoveringFromSlam` as class
A with their real console callers. A sweep you have not watched succeed on a known instance
is not a sweep. [[harness-answers-the-wrong-question]]
